pre._gen_logs_fixed: 11 September 2026: this named out/gen_pcb_c3.log, which no chain has written since full.sh replaced the clones; full.sh writes the placement generator to out/gen3.log. A declared log that is never written blocks every run of the board.

route._layer_rules_removed: REMOVED 8 Sep 2026 17:50: the per-class layer rule (rule 2) cost C8 three routes that never finished a pass (12 min, 90 min, 3 h with nothing written) while the same DSN without it auto-routed in 14 min 21 s; and the D9 read-back this morning showed the router does not hold a class to its layers anyway. The pair pre-router lays the pairs on their layers by construction, which is what enforces the intent now.
route._optimiser_note: 1 pass: the auto-route finishes in about 14 minutes and the default two optimiser passes ran past 90 minutes three times without writing a session (8 Sep 2026)
route._passes_note: 30 passes, not 100: the 3-pass probe took 14 min 21 s, so this board costs about 4.5 minutes a pass at the start and 100 passes cannot finish inside any limit we set; C7 converged before its ceiling and C8 does not (8 Sep 2026 21:10). A session is written only when the whole job ends, so an unreachable ceiling means no result at all.
route._jar_unpinned: 11 September 2026: this pinned ~/bin/freerouting-1.9.0.jar, the STOCK jar, which set FR_JAR and so bypassed route_one's own choice AND its refusal. Our 1.9.0 build writes a session after every pass; the stock one writes one only when the whole job ends, so a run that is cut leaves nothing, which is what every NO_SESSION round in the record is. Unpinned: route_one takes the patched jar when the host has it and refuses when it does not, unless FR_REQUIRE_MESH=0 says otherwise deliberately.
route._ripup_why: 14 September 2026: C12 ended 0 hard with two opens, /PWM1 and /HB2, and both pads sit in open ground (nothing within 2.12 mm of TP29, nothing but its partner's tracks within 1.65 mm of R44). A board-wide stub search at a 0.1 mm grid on all three routing layers, at the panel's own class clearance of 0.127 rather than the tool's old 0.16 literal, finds no path for either: the lanes are not there and no closure will make them. The router is deterministic, so more passes repeat the result and only a different rules file is a different solution. via_costs 100 was round two's remedy and took 12 opens to 4; the rip-up cost is the second lever fr_rules writes and has never been moved on this board. 10 against the default 100 makes the router far more willing to tear up and re-lay, which is what a board whose strips are full needs.

notes: C13, 14 September 2026 (MESHSAT-862): C12's copper routed with the rip-up cost at 10 instead of the default 100, in an isolated tree so the tools can move under the rest of the work. Everything else is C12's.
